instruction: Summarize this abstract in one sentence.

bees.text: A small neural network, using a cheap camera and board, efficiently counts bees at hive entrances, reducing manual labor and improving accuracy compared to existing systems.

river.text: A recurrent network forecasts river levels six hours ahead from rainfall, trained on one river and fine-tuned on another with only three months of data, achieving 2.3-hour early warnings on average for rises over half a meter, outperforming physical models without rainfall forecasts.

plastic.text: The abstract summarizes that sorting plastic waste by its infrared spectrum allows recycling plants to identify six common plastic types, including dark ones, with high accuracy and speed.

leaks.text: Finding leaks in water pipes by listening to sound from fire hydrants, a convolutional network trained on spectrograms detects leaks, and identifies 23 out of 27 that were dug up, with 9 false positives, outperforming traditional methods.

wind.text: Grid operators can use day-ahead wind power forecasts from weather maps by feeding convolutional networks trained on weather models, which improve accuracy by 14% compared to grid points, especially when fronts pass near farms.

leaves.text: A phone camera model trained on lab tomato leaf photos performs poorly on real-time, field-based images of diseased leaves, with early-stage disease causing significant misses.
